system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Working analysis for discussion with Australian counsel; not a substitute for formal legal advice.

---

## 1. Headline view

The Seller's "fair and balanced package" is, on a buyer's reading, a liability regime built to shrink our recourse to roughly 20% of price for 18 months, then switch it off entirely, while leaving three value-affecting items (Riverlark debt, Bluefen consent, DD-005 bonuses) unresolved at Completion and shifting the cost of each onto us.

Two features of the package stand out before any individual clause:

1. **The Seller Update and the Disclosure Letter contradict each other.** The Update says Bluefen consent is "addressed" and Ironquay is "adequate"; the Disclosure Letter candidly says no Bluefen consent exists, no evidence the 11.3 conditions are met, no Ironquay payment receipt or assignment exists, and the Riverlark facility is unpaid with no discharge. The Disclosure Letter is the more reliable document – and it is what we should hold the Seller to. We should quote it back.
2. **The Disclosure Letter is already six weeks stale** (data room cut-off 22 September 2026; today is 6 November 2026). The DD-006 privacy investigation was "preliminary" then. We need a bring-down and an updated status on every open item before signing.

The combined effect of Clauses 8.3, 12.3, 9.3/12.8/20.5 and DL [1.1]–[1.2] is the single most important structural problem: **general disclosure of the entire data room + a constructive-knowledge exclusion + "all limitations apply to all Claims" + exclusive remedy/non-reliance for all Claims.** Read together, almost every known risk is simultaneously (a) disclosed against the warranties, (b) deemed within our knowledge, and (c) if it survives that, capped at 20% and time-barred at 18 months – including title, tax, fraud and the specific indemnities. That is not a market position. Each limb needs to be unwound.

---

## 2. Issue-by-issue analysis

### A. Liability architecture

**A1. Fundamental and title warranties subject to the general cap and 18 months (Seller Update "Fundamental / Title")**
- *Departure:* Capacity and title warranties capped at AUD 4.8m with an 18-month cut-off. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. If title to the shares fails, we have paid AUD 24m for nothing and can recover a fifth of it, and only if we find out within 18 months.
- *Position:* Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, no insolvency, share capital) capped at **100% of price** (or uncapped), surviving for the **statutory limitation period** (6 years in NSW from breach; market practice often fixes 6–7 years), and **carved out of the de minimis and basket**.

**A2. General cap at 20% (Clause 12.1)**
- 20% is at the low end for an Australian mid-market private sale without W&I insurance, particularly given the identified live issues (30% customer concentration risk, unresolved IP title, an open privacy incident). Open with **50%**, settle no lower than **30–35%**, or agree 20% only alongside a buyer-side W&I policy with the Seller contributing to premium and a nil/low retention. Even then, the specific indemnities must sit outside the cap.

**A3. Thresholds (Clause 12.2)**
- De minimis AUD 25,000 (~0.1% of price) is acceptable. Basket AUD 250,000 (~1%) is acceptable in size but it is drafted as a **deductible** ("only the excess… recoverable"). Push for a **tipping basket** (first-dollar recovery once exceeded). Require that **related claims aggregate** for de minimis purposes, and that **fundamentals, tax, and all specific indemnities sit outside both thresholds**.

**A4. 18-month claims period and "all limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (Clause 12.3 / 13)**
- 18 months does not give us two audit cycles. Push for **24 months** for general warranties. Tax warranties and the tax indemnity: **7 years** (the ATO's general amendment period is 4 years from assessment, extended or unlimited for fraud/evasion – 7 years is the conventional proxy). Fundamentals: statutory limitation.
- The "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" default must be **reversed**: limitations apply *only* to general Warranty Claims, and *do not* apply to (i) fraud, dishonesty, wilful concealment; (ii) fundamental warranties; (iii) tax warranties/indemnity; (iv) specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, DD-005, Riverlark, leakage); (v) Seller's completion obligations and covenants; (vi) price adjustment / debt-free-cash-free mechanics. Also require that a claim notified in time survives if proceedings are commenced within, say, 6–9 months of notice (not that proceedings be commenced within the 18 months).

**A5. Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" (Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)**
- This is the sweep-up. As drafted, our only remedy for anything – including breach of a Completion covenant or a specific indemnity – is a capped, time-barred Warranty Claim, and we cannot rely on anything outside the four corners of the SPA.
- *Pushback:* (a) exclusive-remedy clause limited to the warranties only, preserving indemnities, specific performance/injunctive relief, termination rights, and remedies for fraud; (b) express **fraud carve-out from every limitation**; (c) non-reliance acceptable only as a conventional "no reliance on pre-contractual representations other than the Warranties", with no attempt to oust statutory misleading-or-deceptive-conduct remedies (Australian Consumer Law s 18 – a non-reliance clause can be relevant to causation but cannot contract out of the statute, and we should not concede wording that tries). Confirm the Disclosure Letter itself is a document we *can* rely on.

### B. Disclosure and knowledge

**B1. General disclosure of the data room and public registers (Schedule 7; DL [1.1]–[1.2])**
- Disclosing "every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to" in DD-002 to DD-012, plus all "publicly searchable corporate records", means any warranty is qualified by anything anywhere in the data room – including inferences we would have to draw by reading DD-008 and DD-011 "together" (DL [8] actually says this). Reject.
- *Position:* Only matters **fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter itself, with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter**, qualify the warranties. Data room documents qualify only where specifically cross-referenced. Public searches limited to the ASIC company extract, PPSR search and court/insolvency searches **as at an agreed date**, results attached. **No disclosure qualifies the specific indemnities or the fundamental warranties.**
- DL [1.4] (no admission) is standard and acceptable, provided it cannot be used to argue that a matter was *not* fairly disclosed when we later claim under an indemnity.

**B2. Buyer knowledge exclusion including constructive knowledge (Clause 8.3)**
- "Knowledge… of the Buyer or its advisers… including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records" is a constructive-knowledge standard applied to our entire adviser team. Combined with B1, it kills most claims regardless of whether anything was actually disclosed.
- *Position:* Delete. Fallback: **actual knowledge** of a short list of named deal-team individuals, of matters constituting a breach **and** its loss, no imputation of adviser knowledge, no "discoverable from" language, and no application to fundamentals, tax or specific indemnities. Note that an actual-knowledge exclusion still cuts against the known issues below – which is why those must be moved into indemnities/price adjustments rather than left as warranties.

### C. Conditions and Completion deliverables

**C1. Bluefen change-of-control consent (Clause 3 / 6.3; DL [2])**
- ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue. The Update says the consent is "addressed"; the Disclosure Letter says **no final written consent and no evidence the 11.3 conditions are satisfied**. "Reasonable endeavours" plus "treat as satisfied on delivery of written consent" lets any letter – conditional, from the wrong signatory, with pricing concessions – satisfy the condition.
- *Position:* Hard **condition precedent** for the Buyer's benefit, waivable only by us. The consent must be (i) in writing from an authorised Bluefen signatory, (ii) **unconditional** or with all 11.3 conditions satisfied and evidenced, (iii) in a form approved by us, (iv) without amendment to pricing, term, exclusivity or termination rights, (v) delivered before or at Completion. Seller to use **all reasonable endeavours**, with Buyer involvement in Bluefen discussions. Long-stop date with Buyer termination right. If Bluefen imposes commercial concessions or terminates within 12 months citing the change of control, consider a **price adjustment / deferred consideration** linked to Bluefen revenue retention. We need the Bluefen contract's 11.3 conditions in front of us now.

**C2. Riverlark facility ~AUD 3.2m (Clause 2 / 7; DL [3])**
- "Release to be provided following Completion" is incompatible with debt-free/cash-free. At Completion the Company would still owe AUD 3.2m, likely in **default under change-of-control clause 8.1**, with Riverlark's security remaining enforceable over the business – and potentially over the shares we have just bought (see F1). The Seller's covenant strength (a venture vehicle, Pty Ltd) is unknown.
- *Position:* Repayment at Completion out of the purchase price via the **funds flow**, against a **payoff letter** from Riverlark stating the exact discharge amount (including break costs), and delivery at Completion of **executed releases/discharges of all security** (PPSR discharge, release of any mortgage over shares/assets, release of guarantees), or a binding undertaking from Riverlark to lodge the PPSR discharge within [5] business days. Change-of-control waiver if there is any gap. Riverlark debt defined as **Debt** in the completion adjustment so it reduces the headline price.

**C3. Funds flow and DD-005 Completion bonuses AUD 420,000 (DL [5])**
- These are **liabilities of the Company**, triggered by Completion, payable to its employees. "A matter for the Seller and not separately itemised" either means the Company pays them post-Completion (we fund them) or the Seller pays them through Company payroll (which still has tax and super consequences for the Company). Either way they are a **transaction-related debt-like item**.
- *Position:* Include in the funds flow as a **deduction from price** (or paid by Seller before Completion with evidence), **grossed up for on-costs**: superannuation guarantee (12% from 1 July 2025), NSW payroll tax (~5.45% if above threshold), PAYG withholding and any leave accrual impact. Estimate ~AUD 500k+ all-in. Specific indemnity for any shortfall and for any claim that the "continued-employment" conditions were not met in a way that exposes the Company. Confirm whether any bonuses are structured so the Company carries them as retention payments post-Completion – if so, they belong in the debt-like deduction too.

### D. Specific risks with inadequate protection

**D1. Ironquay – SOW3 IP title (Clause 11.1; DL [4])**
- DD-004 cl 7.3: IP in the SOW3 Project Materials only transfers on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. AUD 180,000 is open; no receipt, no confirmatory assignment. Until paid, **the Company does not own that IP** – it sits with a contractor. If that IP is embedded in the analytics product (very likely for an "analytics" business), the real exposure is not AUD 180k; it is infringement risk, re-development cost, an inability to give clean IP warranties to our own customers, and a hold-up position for Ironquay.
- *Position:* Pre-Completion covenant / Completion deliverable: Seller procures **payment of all SOW3 fees** and delivers a **confirmatory deed of assignment** from Ironquay (with moral-rights consents) and Ironquay's written confirmation that nothing further is owed. Specific indemnity extended to **all Loss arising from the Company not owning, or any third-party claim to, the SOW3 Project Materials** – not just the fee – outside the basket and cap (or with its own cap at 100% of price), surviving 6 years. Diligence: confirm there are no other SOWs with the same payment-conditioned transfer; confirm Ironquay has no other IP claims.

**D2. DD-006 export / privacy incident (Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6; DL [6])**
- ~1,240 records of personal information (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) sent to an unintended external address. Under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, where an entity suspects an eligible data breach it must complete an assessment **within 30 days** and notify the OAIC and affected individuals if there is likely serious harm. The investigation was "preliminary" on 22 September; we need to know the incident date and whether that 30-day window has already been breached. Post-2022 penalties for serious/repeated interferences with privacy run to the greater of AUD 50m, 3× benefit or 30% of adjusted turnover, and a statutory tort for serious invasions of privacy is now in force. If the records are **customer data** (e.g. Bluefen end-users), there are likely contractual notification and indemnity obligations to customers as well.
- The Seller's "preliminary… not expected to be material" is an opinion, not a disclosure, and DL [1.4] expressly refuses to concede notification is required.
- *Position:* (i) Pre-signing: obtain the incident log, the recipient's identity, any recall/deletion confirmation, access logs for the download link, and legal advice obtained by the Company; (ii) covenant to **complete the assessment and make any required notifications before Completion**, with Buyer review of the notification; (iii) **specific indemnity** for all Loss arising from the incident (regulatory, customer claims, remediation, notification costs, third-party claims) **uncapped or separately capped at a meaningful level, outside thresholds, surviving 6 years**; (iv) fresh privacy/cyber warranties not qualified by DD-006; (v) consider a **retention/escrow** against this item.

**D3. Sandbar supplier renewals – 3 × AUD 110,000 (DL [8])**
- Three related renewals, each just under what is probably a materiality threshold, which the Seller tells us to "read together". That structure itself warrants scrutiny. We do not know whether they are committed, terminable, prepaid or ordinary course.
- *Position:* Obtain the contracts; confirm whether they are committed pre-Completion and whether termination for convenience exists. Conduct-of-business covenant between signing and Completion requiring Buyer consent for any commitment or renewal over an aggregate (not per-contract) threshold of, say, AUD 100,000 and for any related series of commitments. If prepaid or accrued, treat appropriately in working capital/debt-like adjustments. Warranty that the three renewals are the only such commitments.

**D4. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime"**
- Not accepted. Tax: separate **tax indemnity** for all pre-Completion tax (including the on-costs on DD-005), 7-year survival, 100% cap, outside thresholds. IP: given D1, IP ownership/non-infringement warranties should have at least a 3-year period and a higher cap, and must not be qualified by general disclosure of DD-004.

### E. Lower-order items (verify, don't concede)

- **Office lease (DL [7]):** We should read DD-007 ourselves rather than accept the Seller's characterisation. If it is only a notification obligation, require the Seller to give notice pre-Completion with evidence. Check for any landlord consent requirement triggered by change of control or any guarantee from Harbourglass that needs to be replaced.
- **Mossvale (DL [9]):** A share sale is not usually an "assignment", but definitions vary – check for any change-of-control wording. Require a warranty that **no consents, notices or waivers are required for the transaction other than those listed in a schedule** (Bluefen, Riverlark, lease notice), and that the listed consents are the only ones.

### F. Title

**F1. "Title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012"**
- The register is prima facie evidence, not proof, and DL [10] pointedly says we have not verified it. Required: current ASIC company extract; **PPSR search against the Company and against Harbourglass** (Riverlark's security may well include a mortgage or charge over the shares – if so, the share title itself is encumbered until C2 is resolved); review of the constitution for pre-emptive rights, drag/tag or transfer restrictions; any shareholders' agreement, option, convertible note or ESOP that could dilute "100%". Unconditional title warranties (legal and beneficial owner, no Encumbrances, fully paid, no options) **not qualified by any disclosure**, with the A1 cap/period.

---

## 3. Structural protections to introduce

Given the cap the Seller is proposing and the quality of the open items, we should ask for at least one of:

- **Retention/escrow**: e.g. 10–15% of price held for 24 months, with a specific hold-back tied to DD-006 and Ironquay released on resolution.
- **W&I insurance** as the route to accepting a lower Seller cap – but only with specific indemnities and known issues handled outside the policy (insurers will exclude DD-006, Ironquay and Bluefen as known matters).
- **Parent guarantee / covenant strength evidence** from Harbourglass or its ultimate owner; a venture vehicle may distribute proceeds immediately after Completion.
- **Completion accounts (or locked box with leakage indemnity)** with "Debt" defined to include Riverlark, DD-005 bonuses and on-costs, unpaid Ironquay fees, and any prepaid/accrued Sandbar amounts.
- **MAC / termination right** between signing and Completion, including loss of or material adverse change to the Bluefen relationship and any regulator action on DD-006.
- **Bring-down** of the Disclosure Letter at Completion with a Buyer right to terminate (not merely a right to claim) for material new disclosures.

---

## 4. Summary of recommendations (priority order)

| # | Issue | Our position |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fundamental/title warranties capped at 20% / 18 months | 100% of price (or uncapped); statutory limitation period; outside thresholds; not disclosure-qualified |
| 2 | "All limitations apply to all Claims"; exclusive remedy & non-reliance for all Claims | Limitations apply to general Warranty Claims only; express carve-outs for fraud, fundamentals, tax, specific indemnities, covenants and price mechanics; no attempt to oust ACL remedies |
| 3 | Riverlark AUD 3.2m released "after Completion" | Repaid from funds flow at Completion against payoff letter; security discharges and change-of-control waiver delivered at Completion; defined as Debt |
| 4 | Bluefen consent ("addressed" but not obtained) | Buyer-only-waivable CP: unconditional written consent, 11.3 conditions evidenced, Buyer-approved form, no adverse amendments; all reasonable endeavours; long-stop; consider revenue-linked adjustment |
| 5 | General data-room disclosure + constructive knowledge (Sch 7, DL [1.1]–[1.2], cl 8.3) | Fair and specific disclosure standard only; delete cl 8.3 or limit to actual knowledge of named individuals; no application to fundamentals, tax or indemnities |
| 6 | DD-005 bonuses AUD 420k outside funds flow | Price deduction or Seller-funded pre-Completion, grossed up for super/payroll tax/PAYG; specific indemnity |
| 7 | Ironquay indemnity limited to AUD 180k fee | SOW3 paid and confirmatory IP assignment delivered at Completion; indemnity covers all Loss from IP non-ownership; outside cap/thresholds; 6 years |
| 8 | DD-006 privacy incident "not material" | Full incident file; assessment completed and notifications made pre-Completion; uncapped/separately capped specific indemnity outside thresholds; escrow hold-back |
| 9 | General cap 20%, 18 months, deductible basket | Cap 50% opening / ≥30–35% floor (or 20% + W&I); 24 months general, 7 years tax; tipping basket; related claims aggregate |
| 10 | Tax/IP "under general regime" | Separate tax indemnity (7 years, 100%); IP warranties with longer period and higher cap |
| 11 | Sandbar 3 × AUD 110k | Contracts reviewed; aggregate-based conduct covenant; working capital/debt-like treatment |
| 12 | Title via register only; lease; Mossvale | ASIC/PPSR/constitution checks (watch for Riverlark share security); Seller gives lease notice pre-Completion; "no other consents" warranty with schedule |
| 13 | Stale Disclosure Letter (22 Sept 2026) | Bring-down at signing and Completion; termination right for material new matters |

**Immediate diligence asks to the Seller (this week):** current status letters on Bluefen, Riverlark payoff figure, Ironquay payment/assignment, DD-006 incident chronology and legal advice, DD-005 bonus letters and on-cost workings, the three Sandbar agreements, DD-007 and DD-009 clause extracts, and an ASIC/PPSR search pack.

If helpful, I can turn this into a tracked mark-up of Clauses 3, 6.3, 7, 8.3, 9.3, 11.1, 12 and 13 and Schedule 7, or draft the specific indemnity and funds-flow language.
=== END ADVICE ===
